# Custody check: tasklane

**Your app has 5 answers that are No or Don't know.**
Why this matters: a stranger can reach what your app does not protect. That can be a key, someone else's record, or an admin button. Nothing on screen shows it until someone tries.
This check reads your app's files, your code and your answers. It ends with one door: Ship it, Patch it, or Get a person. Each Don't know is a next question, not a failure.

## Stop-line
Not ticked.

## Next change: add comments on tasks → **Gated**
This change needs extra checks: it touches user data and how your data is stored (a new kind of record). Gates to run: Define, Audit, Plan, Plan review, Build, Verify, Diff review, and a security review.

## Door: **Patch it**
Two of Q4, Q5, Q6 and Q9 are No or Don't know: Q4 is No and Q9 is Don't know.

## Patch list
**1. Any signed-in user can do owner and admin actions (Q4)**
- Changes a person's role. It only checks that someone is signed in, not that they are an admin. `app/api/admin/users/route.ts:10`
- Deletes a project. It only checks that someone is signed in, not that they own the project. `app/api/projects/[id]/route.ts:10`

What could go wrong: any of your 30 users can make themselves an admin, or delete another team's project.
Check it (1 min): Delete a project as its owner and copy that request from the network tab. Sign in as an ordinary user. Send the same request again, changing only the session. It should refuse.

**2. No one gets told when the app breaks (Q9)**
What could go wrong: the app fails for your users, and you find out only when someone complains.
Check it (1 min): In the copy that isn't live, remove one key from its settings. Did anyone get a message? Put it back.

## The eleven
| # | Question | Answer | Confidence | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Secrets out of the browser | Nothing found (scanner) | med | `6 files read: no key in client code, no MCP token, no env file` · `nothing-found-keys` |
| 2 | Client or server | yes (from your code) | med | `app/projects/page.tsx:8`, `app/projects/page.tsx:13`: the browser only asks your server. The writes run on the server at `app/api/tasks/route.ts:10` and `app/api/projects/[id]/route.ts:10` |
| 3 | Who can read this | Nothing found (scanner) | med | `1 rule file read: no RLS disabled, no using (true) policy, no if-true Firebase rule` · `nothing-found-rules` |
| 4 | Who is allowed to do this | no (from your code) | med | `app/api/admin/users/route.ts:10`, `app/api/projects/[id]/route.ts:10` |
| 5 | Code back in five minutes, data from a backup | yes | high | code: yes (you) · data: yes (you) |
| 6 | A copy that isn't live | yes (you) | high | (you) |
| 7 | What changed that I didn't ask for | yes (you) | high | (you) |
| 8 | What one user costs | don't know (you) | low | (you) |
| 9 | How I'd find out it's broken | don't know (you) | low | `4 dependencies read: no error tracking, no Sentry config, no health route, no cron` · `nothing-found-monitoring` |
| 10 | What I'm storing | yes (you) | high | `supabase/migrations/001_init.sql:1` · `pii-field`. You named emails and task titles |
| 11 | Can I export and leave | yes (you) | high | (you) |

Answers marked (scanner) came from the file tree. Answers marked (from your code) came from reading your code, at the `path:line` shown. Answers marked (you) came from your answers block. A scanner or code "yes" is medium confidence until you confirm it.

Note: all three server handlers use a database connection that skips your row level security (the database rule that says who can read each row). So the rules in `supabase/migrations/001_init.sql` do not protect these actions. Each handler must check access itself, and two of them do not.

One place decides who is allowed: don't know (you). Run build-decisions to see each place your app decides it.

## Five, if you'll only do five
1. Classify the next change against the Gated list.
2. Boundary test: logged out, wrong user, right user; on each screen, each saved record and each uploaded file.
3. One full path on the live site, including any background job, email, payment message or AI call.
5. Prove you can go back to the last version, and get one real alert.

## Don't know: the next questions to answer
- **Q1** Secrets out of the browser: Nothing found in the files; the running app is still the question: on your live site, search the loaded files and network responses for `sk-`, `sk_live_`, `service_role`, `AKIA`, `ghp_`, `PRIVATE KEY`. If you find one, rotate it now.
- **Q3** Who can read this: Nothing found in the files; the running app is still the question: in a private window, open a record's address. Then, as user B, request user A's record. Both should refuse.
- **Q8** What one user costs: divide last month's host and AI bills by your user count, then check that a spending cap is set.
- **Q9** How I'd find out it's broken: break one setting in the copy that isn't live and see if anyone gets a message.

I did not ask whether your app calls an AI model, because you asked for no more questions. If it does, the six "Keeping the AI on rails" questions still apply.
